beats.t: Just before the bell, at the Sundial Stage. The sun had been eaten down to a slender crescent. The sundial's pointer had almost lost its shadow.
The three climbed the rear steps. Yeoni's throat was still empty. Moka gripped his ladle so tightly that his paws had gone white.
(Will anyone come?)
How many flyers did you hand out?
(A thousand. All pictures.)
You drew this a thousand times? Your paws must hurt.
Both of you, quiet. Actually, one of you already is.
Cat. Be honest. Do you think this will work?
I don't know.
That's where you're supposed to say yes!
If I say something will work when I don't know, you won't believe me. We try because we don't know.
(Yeongnyangi was kind of cool just now.)
The bell rang. The first bell. The entire island trembled at its sound. Crows perched on every roof over the stage lifted their heads together.
This is a noon-prohibited zone.
All who ascend will be confiscated.
The mask remained cracked. The crow held its head slightly lowered so nothing could be seen through the gap.
C-cat. There's nobody here.
Moka was right. The square below the stage stood empty. Only wind passed through.
(They're too scared to come after all.)
Of course. Obviously. I wouldn't come either. Let's go back.
It's only the first bell. Don't rush.
Then it came. Tap, tap-tap. A box being beaten in an alley at the square's edge.
Captain Drum. Behind him, the old woman. Behind her, the market people. The underground audience too, and Yeoul. Everyone held a pot lid.
(The lid festival!)
...They actually brought lids.
They brought them so you wouldn't be afraid. They didn't come to watch you. They came to join you.
Disperse.
The flock descended over the square. People flinched, but nobody turned away. The old woman stood at the front, holding her lid like a shield.
Those who sing are ridiculed. Did you come not knowing that?
Moka, now!
N-now?
Before the second bell. The first sound.
Moka walked to the center of the stage. His legs felt like wooden sticks. More than a hundred eyes in the square turned to him at once.
He opened his mouth. Nothing came out. No stamp on him. Nothing the crow had eaten.
...I can't. It won't come out.
Yeoni approached from behind with a pot lid. They held it up in front of Moka's face.
(You said it comes out in front of a pot.)
Moka looked at the lid. At his reflected face. And behind it, the pig's smiling face.
Two spoons of soy.
A small voice. Perhaps only the old woman at the front could hear.
One spoon of sweet. Keep the heart gentle and high the heat.
Captain Drum struck the box. Boom, tap-tap. Moka's voice grew a little louder.
Turn the skewers, turn, turn before they burn. Grandma said that life's got turns to learn.
The rhythm tangled. On the final line, Moka's voice cracked with a squeak.
Laughter burst from somewhere in the square. One person. Two. It spread.
See? Ridicule.
(No. If Moka stops—)
Moka stopped. His face went bright red. Then he laughed too. His cracked voice was simply too funny not to.
Oh, ruined it! From the top! Two spoons of soy!
(Moka's laughing. Onstage.)
The square shouted along. Two spoons of soy! Laughing, offbeat, tapping lids.
They aren't laughing at him. They are laughing with him.
It was a song. A chaotic, tuneless song. A recipe followed by a hundred people, each a beat late.
...Why?
The crow's voice trembled. Another crack spread through the mask.
Why is nobody angry? It's wrong. Ridiculous.
(It's good because it's ridiculous.)
Yeoni moved their mouth without sound. The crow saw the shape of those words.
A shining thread unwound from inside the crow's robes. A thread trembling in the shapes of sol and mi. Drawn toward the square's laughter, it flew back into Yeoni's throat.
OIIIIIINK!
Sol to mi. The notes mocked in the courtroom rang through the center of the square.
Let's make that our chorus!
I didn't return it. The thread went by itself.
I know. Thank you anyway.
...Nobody has said thank you to me before.
The second bell rang. The sundial's pointer caught its final shadow. Almost all the sun had been devoured.
Yeoni. Push the sun upward. With song.
Song? My karaoke score is forty-seven.
Exactly. With a forty-seven-point song.
Hey, my voice cracked too. You're not the only one embarrassed.
Is that comfort?
Accounting between accomplices.
Yeoni drew breath. They remembered how their words had become fire in court. Then, they had been angry. Not now.
Become delicious.
Yeoni's voice became an ember. Instead of sharp letters, round lights spread above the square. People's voices took up the fire one by one.
Everyone together! Two spoons of soy!
A hundred embers rose into the sky and touched the edge of the devoured sun. The black shadow flinched as though burned.
The shadow tore. Light poured through. The sundial's pointer planted a short shadow precisely on the ground. Noon.
Then black hands poured from the torn darkness. Their fingers reached neither for people nor the sun, but for one thing alone. The crow.
You have failed, child. I am taking back the feathers.
Please wait. Not yet, I still—
Who are you? Show yourself.
The cat in the hat. Do not hurry. You are not yet my share.
Black hands enveloped the crow. The mask shattered. Behind it was the shadow of a boy holding a microphone.
No!
Yeoni lunged. Their hoof touched the boy's fingertips. Warm. An instant later, those fingertips slipped away like smoke.
I wanted...
I wanted to sing together too.
The black hands vanished into shadow. Only one gray feather remained in Yeoni's hoof.
The sun rose over the island's center. Roofs, alleys, and sea regained their colors. A wave crashed with a splash. A sound unheard for so long.
Gray stamps melted from the hands of people in the square. The old woman opened her mouth. A hoarse voice, but unmistakable words.
She spoke. Just now, she spoke.
What did she say?
That it was delicious. My skewer. Just like my grandmother's.
See? I told you five stars wasn't out of reach.
...Not five yet. Four and a half.
Moka. You're crying.
Oil splashed! In my eyes!
There isn't even a fire lit right now.
Two characters rose from the sundial's pointer. 丙午—Byeong-o. The midday sun and the midday Horse. They seeped into Yeoni's chest.
[ Four Pillars characters recovered · Month Pillar: 丙午 ]
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □□ ]  4/8
Half filled! Only half to go!
The remaining half is harder.
Can you say that later? This is celebration time.
Your Month Pillar. The energy of your season. Byeong is Hurting Officer; Jeong within O is Eating God. You used both today.
Yep. One burned skewers, one grilled them.
Precisely.
Yeoni opened their hoof. The gray feather rested there. Its tip trembled faintly.
I don't even know his name. He said he wanted to sing with us.
He tore down my grandmother's shop sign.
I know. But still.
...Still, we could have sung together. Like today.
A feather remains. That means it isn't over.
The sun began to descend. Properly setting at last. The lotus-leaf boat floated up beside the river, ready for the next island.
Moka. Come with us?
Why would I?
We're accomplices. What kind of accomplice abandons another accomplice?
Don't steal my lines.
Moka wrapped the ember jar in his apron and packed his grandmother's ladle too. Captain Drum followed them to the boat, beating his box. Boom, tap-tap, boom.
I'll guard the ember. You just stay out of trouble.
But trouble is my specialty.
Exactly why I'm saying don't.
The boat rocked. As Yeoni caught the railing, the gray feather slipped from their hoof and rode the wind.
Ah, the feather!
The wind has it. Feathers know their way back.
Where did you learn a line like that?
Just made it up.
Yeoni crouched before Captain Drum. The gold-thread scar still marked his wrist.
Captain Drum. I promise I'll find your name.
He nodded, then struck his box as loudly as he could.
Just before boarding, Yeongnyangi met Moka's eyes. Moka's gaze dropped to his right forepaw.
Noon is over.
I'll tell Yeoni on the next island.
Are cats animals that postpone promises?
Without answering, Yeongnyangi boarded. Beneath his white fur, the wound character had deepened a little.
On the hill, the black tiger sat against the setting sun. Wind carried a gray feather from the square. The one that had left Yeoni's hoof.
A black paw pinned it down. After staring at it a long while, the tiger slipped it inside its cloak.
Raising the sun with a song full of cracked notes. Five stars.
A song without ridicule. If such a thing existed, you could have told me from the beginning.
